headline: Granted variances and special permits for 16 Country Drive, 143 Brimbal Ave, 19 Dodge Street, and 21 Beaver Pond Road additions.
summary: The Zoning Board of Appeals heard several new and continued applications for variances, special permits, and a minor modification, granting most of them by 5-0 votes. The Board also continued two applications to future meetings, approved several sets of past minutes, approved 2026 meeting dates, and approved a fee increase for ZBA applications.
decisions: Granted a Variance at 16 Country Drive to construct a rear addition and deck encroaching 4' into the rear lot line where 25' is required, 5-0.
Granted a Special Permit at 16 Country Drive to construct an addition 10.3' from the side lot line where 15' is required, 5-0.
Found that the proposed change in plans at 143 Brimbal Ave. is a minor modification, 5-0.
Granted the requested Minor Modification at 143 Brimbal Ave., 5-0.
Granted a Special Permit at 19 Dodge Street, Unit 110 for new channel letters with 46.71 sq. ft. of signage, 5-0.
Granted the request to continue the application at 21 Bridge Street to the March 25, 2026 meeting, 5-0.
Granted a Variance at 21 Beaver Pond Road to construct a garage 20' tall where 15' is allowed, 5-0.
Granted the request to continue the application at 12 Tozer Road to the April 22, 2026 meeting, 5-0.
Approved the January 28, 2026 meeting minutes as written, 5-0.
Approved the November 25, 2025 meeting minutes as written, 4-0.
Approved the October 22, 2025 meeting minutes as written, 4-0.
Approved the October 14, 2025 meeting minutes as written, 4-0.
Approved a fee increase for ZBA applications to $200 for regular applications and $250 for administrative appeals, 5-0.
plain_text:
CITY of BEVERLY
Zoning Board of Appeals
February 25, 2026at 7:00 pm
These minutes are not a verbatim transcript of the public hearing of the Board of Appeals.  
Reviews of these Minutes or outcome of the public hearing should include an examination of the 
Board’s decision for that hearing.  
Members Present: Will Cosmas, Chairperson, Michael Barone, Cory Farinella, Laura 
Meisenhelter and Benjamin Roy
Others Present:     Jim Butler, Building Commissioner
Leanna Harris, Administrative Assistant
Location:       Council Chambers City Hall, 191 Cabot Street, Beverly
Will Cosmas began the meeting at 7:04pm and introduced the Board members present.
NEW PUBLIC HEARING
Evan Mazzaglia
requests a Variance and a Special Permit to construct a new 187 sq. ft. addition with a 
connecting 131 sq. ft. deck that will require a Variance to encroach 21’ upon the rear lot line 
where 25’ is required. The home is nonconforming to the side yard setback with 9.9’ to the side 
lot line requiring a Special Permit for the proposed addition to be 10.3’ from the side lot line 
where 15’ is required.  The property is located at 16 Country Drive in the R10 zoning district.  
Evan Mazzaglia addressed the Board and stated he is the homeowner and he is seeking a 
Variance and a Special Permit for his single family raised ranch built in 1965.  The project 
includes constructing a 187 sq. ft. addition and removal of the existing wooden deck to make 
room for a new enlarged living space.  The new 132 sq. ft. wooden deck will be off the west side 
of the new addition and leading to the backyard. Mr. Mazzaglia stated they have two young 
children and are looking to create more active living space.
Mr. Mazzaglia stated they are looking for a Variance under Section 300-34D(5). He stated that 
the proposed project is designed to stay as compact as possible while still giving their family the 
additional space they need.
Mr. Mazzaglia stated he met with their neighbors to discuss the plans with them.  He provided a 
signed petition in support of the project.
Ms. Meisenhelter stated it looks like a lot of the properties in the area are similar and close to the
lot lines.
Page 2 of 7
No one spoke in favor or against.
MOTION:  Mr. Roy moved to close the public hearing. 
Ms. Meisenhelter seconded the Motion.
Votes in favor: 5-0 (Cosmas, Barone, Farinella, Meisenhelter, Roy)
Motion carries.
Mr. Farinella stated it looks like a reasonable request and they are keeping the addition as small 
as possible.
Mr. Roy stated he appreciates the very thorough application they have submitted.  Mr. Roy asked
how they are going to heat the additional space. Mr. Mazzaglia stated likely electric baseboard.  
The existing home has duct work and forced hot air.  It will be on sonar tube foundation.
Mr. Barone stated he thinks it’s a fair request.  The applicant is stuck with only 80’ of depth 
where 100’ is required, otherwise the project would be within the setbacks. The proposed project 
would result in a very minor encroachment.
Mr. Barone asked Mr. Butler what section of the ordinance the Special Permit is seeking relief 
from. 
MOTION:  Mr. Barone moved to GRANT a Variance at 16 Country Drive to construct a
rear addition and proposed deck, encroaching 4’ into the rear lot line where 25’ is 
required on the basis that a hardship is created by both the nonconforming lot and the 
existing location of the house on the lot, subject to the plans submitted.  
Mr. Farinella seconded the Motion.
Votes in favor: 5-0 (Cosmas, Barone, Farinella, Meisenhelter, Roy)
Motion carries.
MOTION: Mr. Farinella moved to GRANT a Special Permit at 16 Country Drive to 
construct an addition to be 10.3’ from the side lot line where 15’ is required, subject to the
plans submitted.  Ms. Meisenhelter seconded the Motion.
Votes in favor: 5-0 (Cosmas, Barone, Farinella, Meisenhelter, Roy)
Motion carries.
MODIFICATION
Original Request:
Glovsky & Glovsky o/b/o Vittori-Rocci Post 56 and Italian American War Vets
In a petition for a request for a Special Permit/Finding to authorize a 3 story, 13,158 sq. ft.
addition to an existing nonconforming building in the IR/IR Overlay District. The existing
nonconforming situation includes a 1.25 acre lot where 2 acres is required, a 19.4 foot front yard
setback where 30 feet is required, an 18 foot setback where 20 feet is required and a lot coverage
ratio (building and impervious surface) of 85.9% where 60% is the maximum allowed. The new
Page 3 of 7
addition will comply with all applicable setback and height requirements. The property is
located at 143 Brimbal Avenue in the IR and IR Overlay District.
** Applicant is seeking a Minor Modification
Conor Walsh, Esq. (Glovsky & Glovsky) stated the applicant is seeking a modification of the 
approved plans related to the relief granted by the Board in 2021.
MOTION:  Mr. Barone moved to table this application and move it to the end of the 
agenda.  Mr. Roy seconded the Motion.
Votes in favor: 5-0 (Cosmas, Barone, Farinella, Meisenhelter, Roy)
Motion carries.
[5 minute recess]
Conor Walsh, Esq. (Glovsky & Glovsky) stated this Board granted a Special Permit dated 
September 30, 2021 allowing a change of use to a new retail use and to authorize the expansion 
of the nonconforming structure with an approximate 12,000 sq. ft. addition.  The Board had 
concluded that the change in use satisfied the Special Permit criteria.  However, a nearby 
property owner appealed that decision and the litigation resulted in the favor of the applicant.  
The deadline for this 2021 Special Permit tolled during that litigation.
Atty. Walsh stated that the applicant now seeks a minor modification based on a reduction in the 
scale of the project. The minor modification concerns a proposed 400 sq. ft. loading dock. 
According to Atty. Walsh, the parking area has been revised and there will be more than the 
required parking at the premises. He stated that the applicant revised its plans because 
construction costs have risen considerably since 2021 and the applicant also has spent hundreds 
of thousands of dollars in litigation related to the 2021 Zoning Board decision. 
Mr. Barone asked if the building is currently being used for retail and Mr. Arcari stated it is being
used for storage of rugs.
Mr. Farinella asked who appealed the Zoning Board decision and Atty. Walsh stated 133 
Brimbal Ave.  
Mr. Barone questioned if the use is ongoing and the development of the addition is only 400 sq. 
ft. wouldn’t it just require a building permit since 400 sq. ft. is definitely less than 25% of the 
building square footage.  Atty. Walsh stated the decision was subject to the plans submitted in 
2021 and now those plans have changed.
No one spoke in favor or against.
MOTION: Mr. Roy moved to close the public hearing.
Mr. Barone seconded the Motion.
Votes in favor:  5-0 (Cosmas, Barone, Farinella, Meisenhelter, Roy)
Motion carries.
Page 4 of 7
Thad Siemasko (SV Design) addressed the Board and provided an overview of the plans.  Mr. 
Siemasko stated that the applicant is not adding any volume to the existing building, and the 
second floor has been removed from the plans.
Mr. Barone stated the revised plans are minor since it is a reduction in scale.  The nature of the 
use would not be changing.
MOTION: Mr. Barone moved to the Board to find that the proposed change in plans, 
based on the plans submitted, is a minor modification.  Mr. Roy seconded the Motion.
Votes in favor:  5-0 (Cosmas, Barone, Farinella, Meisenhelter, Roy)
Motion carries.
MOTION: Mr. Barone moved to GRANT the requested Minor Modification at 143 
Brimbal Ave. on the basis that the modified plans are not substantially more detrimental 
than the originally proposed and approved plans, subject to the plans submitted.  
Ms. Meisenhelter seconded the Motion.
Votes in favor:  5-0 (Cosmas, Barone, Farinella, Meisenhelter, Roy)
Motion carries.
CONTINUED PUBLIC HEARINGS
Keara Healy o/b/o Beverly Plaza LLC
requests a Special Permit to propose a new set of channel letters at Russell Cellular/Verizon 
with a square footage of 46.71' which is greater than what is currently allowed by the Zoning 
Ordinance.  The property is located 19 Dodge Street, Unit 110 in the CG zoning district.
Ryan Fisher addressed the Board on behalf of the applicant and stated the applicant has received 
a letter of recommendation from the Design Review Board dated February 6, 2026 approving the
applicant’s proposal.  The applicant is proposing just over 46 sq. ft. for signage.  Mr. Fisher 
stated that there are two other businesses in the same shopping plaza with similar sized signage. 
The existing Verizon sign will be filled in with the new signage that is the same size, the 
proposed letters just will be larger than what is allowed.
Mr. Cosmas stated that the Board’s decisions are not precedential. Mr. Cosmas asked if this is to 
match Verizon’s change in branding and Mr. Fisher confirmed. Mr. Cosmas asked if the sign 
panel is the same size. Mr. Fisher confirmed and stated it is just the letters that are larger.
No one spoke in favor or against.
MOTION:  Mr. Roy moved to close the public hearing. 
Mr. Farinella seconded the Motion.
Votes in favor: 5-0 (Cosmas, Barone, Farinella, Meisenhelter, Roy)
Motion carries.
Page 5 of 7
Mr. Barone stated this application was well received by the Design Review Board (DRB). He 
added that the consensus of the DRB is that the zoning ordinance allowance doesn’t match the 
size of the frontage of the stores 
MOTION:  Mr. Roy moved to GRANT a Special Permit at 19 Dodge Street, Unit 110 to
propose a new set of channel letters at Russell Cellular/Verizon with a square footage of 
46.71' which is greater than what is currently allowed by the Zoning Ordinance, subject 
to the plans submitted and as approved by the Design Review Board.
Ms. Meisenhelter seconded the Motion.
Votes in favor: 5-0 (Cosmas, Barone, Farinella, Meisenhelter, Roy)
Motion carries.
Jason Irving/21 Bridge Street LLC
request a Variance to subdivide the lot, retain the existing single-family home and subdivide the 
existing lot to create a new second lot for the construction of an additional single-family home.  
The addition of another single-family home to the lot would be consistent with the general 
character and other lot sizes in the neighborhood.  The property is located at 21 Bridge Street in 
the R10 zoning district.   
Lisa McGloin, Esq. submitted a written request to continue the meeting to the March 25, 2026, 
meeting, together with the signed applicant waiver.
MOTION:  Ms. Meisenhelter moved to GRANT the request to continue the application 
at 21 Bridge Street to the March 25, 2026 meeting. Mr. Roy seconded the Motion.
Votes in favor: 5-0 (Cosmas, Barone, Farinella, Meisenhelter, Roy)
Motion carries.
Glovksy & Glovsky o/b/o Roy L. Ruff, M.D. and Myra Ruff, Trustees of the 
Myra Ruff Trust and of the Roy L. Ruff Trust
request a Variance to reduce side yard setback requirements from 20’ to 13.4’ and to increase 
maximum size from 100 sq. ft. to approximately 805 sq. ft. and maximum height from 10’ to 
approximately 20’, all to enable the construction of a detached 35’x23’ garage as depicted on 
plans filed with the application.  The property is located at 21 Beaver Pond Road in the R45 
zoning district.  
Conor Walsh, Esq. (Glovsky & Glovsky) stated the applicants are still overseas and are unable to
join the meeting tonight.  The application seeks a Variance for a detached garage. Atty. Walsh 
stated that the subject property is the last house accessed by the private way.  According to Atty. 
Walsh, the applicant and the design team have reconfigured the plans where the garage now 
meets the 20’ side set back requirement and therefore the applicant no longer needs a variance 
for the size of the proposed garage. The applicants now seek a Variance for the structure to be 
20’ high where 15’ is the maximum height allowed. Atty. Walsh stated that the property has 
wetlands in both the front and rear of the property as well as a pool and a septic system.  Atty. 
Walsh stated, at the last meeting, the Board had inquired for the need of an additional garage, and
Page 6 of 7
he informed the Board that the applicant collects classic cars.  The architect has designed the 
garage to have 20’ of height to stylistically match the house and also for the potential installation 
of solar panels. 
Atty. Walsh stated the immediate abutter had submitted a letter in favor of the project at the 
January meeting.
Mr. Barone stated he has reviewed the minutes from the January 28, 2026 meeting.
Mr. Roy stated he appreciates the revised plans.  Ms. Meisenhelter agreed and thanked him for 
making the changes. Mr. Cosmas stated applicants who use continuances to work with the 
Board’s feedback should be applauded.
Mr. Barone stated, seeing the revised plans, the first thing that caught his attention was the 
existing septic location and all the wetlands. There really isn’t another place to put a garage. Mr. 
Barone further stated he doesn’t find a 20’ garage offensive.
MOTION:  Mr. Cosmas moved to GRANT a Variance at 21 Beaver Pond Road to 
construct a garage that is 20’ tall where 15’ is allowed due to the shape and topography of
the land and a literal enforcement of the zoning ordinance would cause substantial 
hardship to the applicant, subject to the revised plans submitted dated 2/12/2026.  
Mr. Farinella seconded the motion.
Votes in favor: 5-0 (Cosmas, Barone, Farinella, Meisenhelter, Roy)
Motion carries.
Cellco Partnership d/b/a Verizon Wireless and the Towers, LLC 
requests a Special Permit under §§300-42 (C)(1)(p) and 300-91 height and setback Variances 
from §300-25A to permit a wireless communications facility with a monopole 124 feet in height 
(including 4' lightning rod) and setback from the property line of approximately 52'.  The 
property is located at 12 Tozer Road in the IR zoning district, Map 68, Parcel 25B.  
The applicant has submitted a written request to continue the meeting to the April 22, 2026, 
meeting, together with the required applicant waiver.
MOTION:  Mr. Cosmas moved to GRANT the request by the applicants to continue the 
application concerning the property at 12 Tozer Road to the April 22, 2026 meeting. Mr. 
Farinella seconded the Motion.
Votes in favor: 5-0 (Cosmas, Barone, Farinella, Meisenhelter, Roy)
Motion carries.
OTHER BUSINESS
A. Approval of January 28, 2026 Meeting Minutes (Cosmas)
MOTION: Mr. Farinella moved to approve the January 28, 2026 meeting minutes, as
Page 7 of 7
written.  Ms. Meisenhelter seconded the Motion.
Votes in favor: 5-0 (Cosmas, Barone, Farinella, Meisenhelter, Roy)
Motion carries.
B. Approval of November 25, 2025 Meeting Minutes (Cosmas)
MOTION: Mr. Roy moved to approve the November 25, 2025 meeting minutes, as 
written.  Mr. Barone seconded the Motion.
Votes in favor: 4-0 (Cosmas, Barone, Farinella, Roy)
Motion carries.
C. Approval of October 22, 2025 Meeting Minutes (Cosmas)
MOTION:  Ms. Meisenhelter moved to approve the October 22, 2025 meeting minutes, 
as written.  Mr. Farinella seconded the Motion.
Votes in favor: 4-0 (Cosmas, Barone, Farinella, Meisenhelter)
Motion carries.
D. Approval of October 14, 2025 Meeting Minutes (Barone)
MOTION:  Mr. Barone moved to approve the October 14, 2025 meeting minutes, as 
written.  Mr. Cosmas seconded the Motion.
Votes in favor: 4-0 (Cosmas, Barone, Farinella, Meisenhelter)
Motion carries.
E. Approval of 2026 Meeting Dates (Harris)
MOTION:  Mr. Roy moved to approve the proposed 2026 meeting dates. 
Mr. Farinella seconded the Motion.
Votes in favor: 5-0 (Cosmas, Barone, Farinella, Meisenhelter, Roy)
Motion carries.
F. Approval of fee increase for ZBA applications (Butler)
MOTION: Ms. Meisenhelter moved to approve the proposed application fee increase to 
$200 for regular applications and $250 for administrative appeals.  
Mr. Roy seconded the Motion.
Votes in favor: 5-0 (Cosmas, Barone, Farinella, Meisenhelter, Roy)
Motion carries.
MOTION:  Ms. Meisenhelter moved to adjourn the meeting at 8:45pm.  
Mr. Barone seconded the Motion.
All in favor.
Motion carries.
Leanna Harris, Administrative Assistant
        Board of Appeals of the Zoning Ordinance
